title: Thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH)

review.note: Drafted from the source below; not yet reviewed by a medical professional.

measures: TSH is a hormone made by the pituitary gland that tells the thyroid how much thyroid hormone to make. A TSH blood test measures how well the thyroid is working.
context: TSH can be higher or lower even with a healthy thyroid. Pregnancy, some other illnesses not related to the thyroid, being over age 80, and certain medicines can all affect the level, so one result alone does not confirm a thyroid condition.
aboveRange: Can be associated with an underactive thyroid (too little thyroid hormone)
May be higher in people over about age 80 who have no thyroid problem
Rarely, may relate to a pituitary gland problem
belowRange: Can be associated with an overactive thyroid (too much thyroid hormone)
May be lower for a short time during some other illnesses
May be a little low in early pregnancy
nextStep: Discuss this result with your doctor.
